_notes: The Unpicked, wearing her red. The fight that cannot be won, what is left afterwards, and the title card.
Scenes 26-32 of the prologue as it was before the split; `--scene story:<index>` still counts across the whole prologue, not within this file.

coach.text: MOONLIGHT — the pale card, and hers. It is WILD: one Moonlight pays any cost you own, whatever colour the pips are. Everything she made worked on anything.
Her room is still helping. Moonlight costs one less in here, which is the last thing she does for you.
And when the hand is empty: CONCENTRATE. The whole turn for one spent card back, arriving next turn.

hints.1: Moonlight is hers, and it is WILD — a Moonlight card pays for anything you own. Spend it. Spend everything.
hints.5: Her room makes Moonlight cheaper. She is still helping. It still will not be enough.

lines: Hearing came back first. Floorboards under one cheek, the smell of cold hearth. Four paws — count them — four.
Whatever had been standing in the doorway is not standing in the doorway. Get up, Ash.
Elspeth in her chair. The light gone out of her hands.
The kettle was still screaming. It had been screaming this whole time, and I did not hear it until now. She hates it when it does that.
I took it off the fire. One paw, the way I had watched her do it ten thousand times from the hearthrug. It took three tries. Nobody will ever know.
I got up on the arm of her chair, which I am not allowed to do, and nobody told me to get down. Her face was not frightened, and not surprised, and not anything.
Between a kettle boiling and a kettle screaming is no time at all. Whoever did this did it in that, in her own parlor, in her own light. Faster than any needle honestly goes.
She always came to the window.
I do not know how to be a cat that nobody is expecting.
I stayed on the arm of the chair a long time, and the shutters stayed shut. Her red kerchief lay folded on the sewing table, washed that morning, waiting to go back around her neck.
I put my head through it. Nobody tied it. It stays.

The thread at my chest, the tether every familiar wears, hers, cut like everything else in this house. Not quite. One strand left, thin as spite, running out from under the window and down into the fog.
Outside, eight bells rang somewhere, and no ninth. The strand runs down into the fog. Then that is where we are going.
